items.title: Silicon Valley elites 'bankrolled' news platform Visegrad24 publishing pro-Israel content: report
items.description: An extensive investigation by American magazine Wired revealed on Thursday how an “anti-migrant, pro-Israel propaganda machine” took form and gained traction via bankrolling by Silicon Valley elites. The investigative report, published by Wired on Thursday morning, detailed the rise of the Polish right-wing news media platform Visegrad24 and how its founder, Stefan Tompson, deliberately engineered a pro-Israel editorial stance to make money from influential supporters, rapidly coming to “dominate” breaking-news discussion of the conflict in Gaza on social media platform X after the attack by Hamas on Oct 7, 2023. The account, at the time three years old, worked “around the clock to pump out nearly 400 posts” on the attacks within three days after Oct 7: “a mix of terse news updates, soft tributes to Israeli victims, and — above all — rage-bait videos showing allegedly ‘pro-Hamas’ demonstrations in cities across the West”, the report said. These racked up 370 million views, launching it into the spotlight overnight as “one of the most influential” pro-Israel accounts on X. Dawn has not independently verified the information or internal correspondence mentioned in the Wired report. Texts reviewed by Wired from Tompson to an anonymous colleague 15 days after the attack indicated that the Visegrad24 founder was already wary that Israel was angling for a wider regional conflict, writing, “The Israelis do seem to be doing some vicious things.” Nevertheless, it revealed, “the founder reasoned a way through his qualms”, messaging the same colleague later the same day to detail his logic on arriving at an “editorial line” on Israel. “As Tompson saw it, V24 had been faced with ‘four options’ once the war started,” Wired reported, quoting him as follows: 1. Say nothing; 2. Be objective — get hated by both sides; 3. Pro Muslim — there are 1.5 billion of them; 4. Pro Israel — There are fewer but also they have a lot of influence and money. Tompson here admitted that his “goal is to fundraise off of this”, the report added, noting that he succeeded according to “an extensive trove of V24 financial records, internal communications, screenshots from group chats, and correspondence with donors”. Wired added that the documents it obtained were responded to by Tompson “with a blanket denial and an email from a lawyer”, and that he did not agree to an interview with the magazine when they declined to send him the questions in advance. “The documents […] reveal how the right kind of online influence, even when it’s strategically acquired by an entity just barely above the gutter of white nationalism, can command support from some of the most powerful people in the world,” the report read. According to the report, messages to the colleague in November 2023 revealed that Tompson was added to two groups “that actively push back against founders who have supported Palestine”. One of these, named Jewish Alliances, was described as a space to “bring together” those working to fight anti-Semitism, and the V24 founder was recommended by a general partner at Sequoia Capital, Shaun Maguire, who Wired claimed had helped to connect the Israel Defence Forces with Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communication network. The other group, an informal WhatsApp thread, consisted of “hundreds of the most powerful figures from Silicon Valley, Wall Street, and Hollywood” discussing how to build support for Israel after the Oct 7 attacks, according to a Puck newsletter. These group chats engaged in activities such as buying domains with pro-Palestinian phrases to “redirect to appropriate content”, such as longlivetheintifada.com and palestineisourhome.com. According to Wired, “the two group chats appear to have paid off pretty handsomely for Visegrad24 ” in terms of fundraising, with Tompson revealing in messages to his colleague (with matching financial records) that donations were rolling in from major investment firms such as Ribbit Capital. Notifications from the website GiveButter , which he used to solicit contributions, show other donations “linked to email addresses associated with” presidents, co-founders, CEOs and heavyweights at various other major companies, including SimpleVenue CEO Michael Sinensky, Warby Parker founder Neil Blumenthal, Wix president Nir Zohar, Lux Capital cofounder Josh Wolfe, and deep tech venture capitalist Matt Ocko. The parties named either declined to comment, claimed to have no records of the donations, or declined to confirm while arguing that V24 did not count as a “far-right” group, according to the magazine. Nevertheless, “over a million dollars” in donations poured in for the organisation, with the magazine reporting that “much of the money, including some of the largest sums, appears to have come in through ‘donor advised funds’ — ‘dark money’ philanthropic vehicles that allow donors to hide their identities, even from the recipients of their cash”. These donations included $175,000 from DonorsTrust, “a fund closely aligned with the Trump administration’s priorities, often referred to as the ‘dark money ATM’ of the American right”, it said. Wired also reported that Tompson encouraged his colleague to “play both sides” by taking opportunities to raise funds from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. “I do the Jewish side. You do Arabs,” he allegedly wrote. According to the report, V24, founded in 2020, gained traction after its “intense volume” of coverage of the Russian invasion of Ukraine — as well as “international notoriety for spreading fake news”, with many of its claims being debunked. It added that Tompson also denied that he was given money for the organisation by the Polish state, although Polish news outlets reported that the prime minister had tried to allocate “about $300,000” to the project in 2022 and “a bit under $600,000” in 2023, sending it to “a sports and fitness NGO” that appeared to be a “carve-out for a V24 -affiliated project”. Later, when Israel launched an attack on Iran in 2025, V24 took a stance of “enthusiasm” for restoring the leadership of Reza Pahlavi and even posted to “influence” US President Donald Trump to join the attack, it said. The success of V24 saw Tompson interviewed by Michael Eisenberg in 2024, an American-born Israeli venture capitalist “often billed as an informal adviser to Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu”, it said.

items.title: Driving Change: German Development Cooperation and partners launch partnership to increase employment opportunities for women in Ghana’s heavy transport and mining sectors
items.description: The German Development Cooperation and Scania West Africa have joined hands to improve professional opportunities and employability of women in Ghana’s heavy transport sector with a particular focus on the mining industry. Through targeted skills development, industry partnerships and job placement support, the project seeks to create a new talent pool of skilled female drivers for one of Ghana’s most important economic sectors. By developing a new pipeline of qualified women drivers and connecting them directly to employers, the Empowering Women in Mining Transport project aims to improve road safety, strengthen productivity for mining companies and contractors, and create decent jobs in an industry where women have historically been excluded. The project is implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and jointly funded through the develoPPP programme together with Scania West Africa Ltd., and in partnership with Reach for Change and Women in Mining. Through this initiative, 80 women will be trained and certified as professional heavy-duty truck drivers, while 200 women will receive complementary training in entrepreneurship, digital literacy, workplace safety, mining operations and sexual harassment prevention Ghana’s mining industry depends on an extensive network of transport and logistics services. Professional truck drivers play an important role in moving materials, supporting operations, and maintaining efficient supply chains. Yet women remain underrepresented in heavy-duty driving and other technical occupations associated with the sector. The project seeks to expand access to these careers by providing women with the professional training and complementary skills required to pursue employment opportunities in a traditionally male-dominated industry. The project reflects Germany’s commitment to partnerships that connect private-sector capabilities with practical development objectives. Through the develoPPP programme, businesses and development partners work together to address development challenges while contributing to sustainable economic activity. Speaking at the launch, the Head of Cooperation at the German Embassy, Johanna Klotz, noted, “Development cooperation is most effective when it creates opportunities that last beyond the life of a project. By bringing German expertise and private-sector engagement together, this partnership aims to turn women’s potential into professional qualifications, decent employment, and lasting economic opportunity”. A central feature of the initiative is its emphasis on measurable employment outcomes. Rather than focusing exclusively on training completion, the project aims to ensure that participants can translate their new qualifications into real jobs. For GIZ, this focus builds on wider efforts in Ghana to strengthen technical and vocational skills, support entrepreneurship, and improve women’s access to economic opportunities. The Country Director of GIZ, Sandra Retzer, noted, “Training must lead somewhere. Our ambition is not simply to equip women with certificates, but to connect their skills to decent jobs and sustainable careers. Success will be measured by the opportunities women can access, the incomes they can earn, and the future they can build.” Professional truck driving requires technical competence, discipline, sound judgement, and a commitment to safety. These are professional standards that apply regardless of gender, and the project is preparing the individual women for just that. The Managing Director of Scania West Africa, Francois Lechat, stated also at the launch, “At Scania, we believe that a more diverse transport sector is a stronger transport sector. Through this partnership, we are investing in women with the skills, confidence and qualifications needed to succeed in careers that have traditionally been inaccessible to them. By working together with our partners, we are helping build a more inclusive and sustainable future for Ghana’s transport and mining industries.” The Empowering Women in Mining Transport initiative represents a step towards a more inclusive and skilled workforce for Ghana’s heavy transport and mining sectors, connecting women’s economic empowerment with industry needs and opportunities for sustainable development.

items.title: Qui est Slimane Hachi, le « Monsieur archéologie » nommé par Tebboune ?
items.description: Pour diriger l’Agence nationale d'archéologie nouvellement créée, le président de la République Abdelmadjid Tebboune a choisi une sommité de la spécialité : Slimane Hachi, éminent archéologue et anthropologue, spécialiste de la préhistoire, particulièrement de l'Algérie et de l'Afrique du Nord. Abdelmadjid Tebboune a nommé un homme au long vécu sur le terrain doublé d’un bagage académique remarquable. À 72 ans, il a l'expérience nécessaire et encore suffisamment d’énergie pour mener à bien une telle mission. Slimane Hachi, expérience de terrain et bagage académique M. Hachi n’est pas un illustre inconnu. Docteur en préhistoire dès 1987 à Aix-en-Provence (France), il a passé plus de 40 ans à traquer les moindres vestiges de l’histoire lointaine de l’Algérie, à partager ses connaissances via des publications et même à diriger des institutions dédiées au patrimoine archéologique . La mission accordée à Slimane Hachi revêt une grande importance pour les autorités. La preuve, le président de la République a tenu à présider lui-même la cérémonie de son installation, mercredi 18 novembre. L’agence est rattachée directement à la présidence de la République. Elle est, entre autres, chargée de définir et de chapeauter la politique nationale de recherche en archéologie. L’Algérie veut déterrer les trésors de son passé millénaire et en faire un outil au service de son rayonnement, de sa place dans le concert des nations et de l'ancrage de son identité. Slimane Hachi est tout indiqué pour orienter les efforts. “L’Algérie, une terre des commencements”, disait Slimane Hachi “L’Algérie n’est pas une terre de passage, mais une terre des commencements (…) à la fois mémoire et matrice de l’humanité”, une terre qui a vu “la naissance du regard symbolique et de l’expression artistique de l’homme”, disait-il. L'allusion est aux gravures rupestres du sud du pays, qui comptent parmi les plus anciennes au monde et qui témoignent d’une présence humaine continue pendant au moins 12 000 ans, voire plus. Des vestiges disséminés aux quatre coins du pays témoignent aussi des différentes époques et civilisations qui ont jalonné l’histoire de l’Algérie pendant les siècles et les millénaires. Slimane Hachi est né en 1954, une année très symbolique pour l'histoire du pays, à Béni Yenni, dans la wilaya de Tizi-Ouzou, une région qui a tant contribué à cette même histoire. Il a été formé à l'archéologie à l’université d’Aix-en-Provence, où il a soutenu en 1987 une thèse de doctorat intitulée “Les Industries d'Afalou Bou Rhummel” (dans la région des Babors), sous la direction du préhistorien français Gabriel Champs, un grand spécialiste de l’histoire des Berbères. Slimane Hachi, un spécialiste de la préhistoire et de l'art rupestre de l'Algérie Pendant plus de 40 ans, les recherches de « Monsieur archéologie » ont porté sur la préhistoire de l'Algérie et de toute l’Afrique du Nord, avec notamment des travaux remarquables sur l’art rupestre du Tassili et du Hoggar. Parmi ses ouvrages, figurent “Préhistoire de l'Ahaggar (Algérie) : l'art rupestre de la Téfedest” (2004), “Les cultures de l'Homme de Mechta-Afalou : le gisement d'Afalou Bou Rhummel” (2003) et “Aux origines des arts premiers en Afrique du Nord : les figurines et les objets modelés en terre cuite de l'abri-sous-roche préhistorique d'Afalou Babors, Algérie” (2003). Il est en outre l’auteur de nombreux articles publiés depuis le début des années 1980 dans les revues spécialisées les plus prestigieuses. Tout en dirigeant le Centre national de recherches préhistoriques , anthropologiques et historiques (CNRPAH), Hachi a régulièrement mis la main à la pâte dans les différents dossiers présentés ces dernières années par l’Algérie à l’Unesco pour faire inscrire et protéger son patrimoine historique. L'archéologue est de ceux qui croient que “l’inscription augmente la visibilité” des éléments du patrimoine algérien. L’article Qui est Slimane Hachi, le « Monsieur archéologie » nommé par Tebboune ? est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Apam, Aggrey Memorial SHS students among passengers injured in Kasoa-Winneba Highway crash
items.description: Students from Apam Senior High School and Aggrey Memorial Senior High School are among several passengers injured in a road crash at Gomoa Dominase Junction on the Kasoa-Winneba Highway. The passengers were travelling in a Sprinter bus with registration number GW 2208-25 when the vehicle crashed at the junction. According to the driver, a taxi made an abrupt U-turn at the junction, distracting him as he approached. He said he tried to avoid hitting the taxi, but one of the Sprinter bus’s rear tyres burst, causing him to lose control of the vehicle. The injured passengers were rushed to the Potsin Polyclinic, where they are receiving treatment. The crash comes after another accident at nearby Gomoa Potsin Junction, where an elderly man was knocked down by a vehicle. The man was also taken to Potsin Polyclinic, treated and discharged.

items.title: We will be heavy on compliance to achieve 2027 tax target – GRA Boss
items.description: Commissioner-General of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), Anthony Kwasi Sarpong, has revealed that the Authority plans to place greater emphasis on compliance to help achieve its tax revenue target for 2027. He also noted that the ongoing VAT reforms, together with the gains made in digitalisation, would significantly support revenue collection going into 2027. The Commissioner-General disclosed this on PM EXPRESS Business Edition, hosted by George Wiafe on JoyNews on November 19, 2026. Concerns and Background The assurance by the Commissioner-General of the Ghana Revenue Authority comes at a time when concerns have been raised that the government could struggle to meet its tax collection target of about GHC 266 billion. Some have also argued that the prevailing global economic uncertainty could affect businesses and their ability to meet their tax obligations. However, speaking on PM EXPRESS, the Commissioner-General said that, based on the Authority’s performance in 2026, it does not consider 2027 a challenge. He added that “we are hopeful that we can raise the required revenue to support the government’s new economy programme.” On the government’s promise to review the VAT rate downwards if there is a high level of compliance after one year, Mr. Sarpong argued that the Finance Minister had not abandoned the commitment. He noted that “we are still looking forward to seeing how things will materialise this year, then the necessary recommendations sent to the finance minister.” Revenue Performance in 2026 Mr. Sarpong also disclosed that the Ghana Revenue Authority is on course to achieve its revenue target for the full year 2026. This follows the Authority’s performance in the first ten months of the year, during which it collected GH¢185.5 billion against a target of GH¢184.4 billion. He said the collection represented a GH¢1.1 billion surplus over the January to October target, with the Authority also surpassing the total revenue of GH¢182 billion recorded in 2025. Emphasising the achievement, the Commissioner-General of the Ghana Revenue Authority said it was recorded in a year when “there were no new taxes, and even government went ahead to abolish some taxes.” He noted that, with two months to go, “we are optimistic that we will end in 2026, exceeding the full-year target.” “We cannot forget about the stability of the economy and how that has impacted businesses honouring their tax obligations to the state,” Mr. Sarpong added.

items.title: Engage us in affordable housing projects – IET-Ghana tells government
items.description: The Institution of Engineering and Technology, Ghana (IET-Ghana), has called on the government to actively engage local engineering professionals in the implementation of major national infrastructure projects, including the government’s Big Push initiative. The call was made as the institution marked its 40th anniversary under the theme, “ Engineering Excellence for Sustainable National Development ”. The President of IET-Ghana, Davor Wonder, urged the government to tap into the expertise and technical capacity of Ghanaian engineers, particularly in the areas of housing, energy, water and road infrastructure. He stressed that the institution had the human resource capacity to contribute meaningfully to national development and should be given practical opportunities to participate in major government projects. “Honourable Minister, we at IET-Ghana have the manpower. Engage us practically in housing, energy, water and road infrastructure. We are always ready to be engaged,” he stated. Mr Davor also underscored the importance of professional ethics and safety in engineering practice, insisting that engineers must prioritise public safety over financial gains. “Technology without responsibility is dangerous. As engineers, we must say no when a project is not safe, even if it is profitable,” he cautioned. Responding to the call, the Minister for Works, Housing and Water Resources, Ahmed Ibrahim, challenged the engineering community to develop innovative and practical solutions to Ghana’s development challenges, particularly the fight against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. He questioned the effectiveness of relying on traditional approaches to tackling the menace, arguing that engineers must be at the forefront of developing sustainable technical interventions. “We can’t be fighting galamsey the old way. Our engineers must provide the solution. You are taught to provide the solution,” the Minister said. Mr Ibrahim further raised concerns about the premature deterioration of infrastructure projects and compromises in technical standards, warning that Ghana could no longer afford investments that failed to deliver their intended benefits. “We can no longer afford a situation where projects fail prematurely, infrastructure does not deliver its intended purpose, or technical standards are compromised,” he stressed. According to the Minister, engineering excellence should not be measured merely by the completion of projects but by their durability, quality and long-term contribution to national development. The 40th-anniversary celebration has renewed calls for stronger collaboration between the government and local engineering professionals, with both sides highlighting the need to put Ghanaian expertise at the centre of infrastructure delivery and sustainable development.

items.title: Diffa/N’Gourti : Yogo inaugure son marché hebdomadaire, un nouveau carrefour d’échanges commerciaux et de fraternité entre le Niger et le Tchad
items.description: Après kossotori, il y a une dizaine de jours, le département de ngourti vient d’être doté d’un second marché, cette fois ci à yogo à l’extrême est du pays, à la frontière tchadienne. Le Secrétaire général adjoint du Gouvernorat de Diffa, M. Mamane Gouzaé, a procédé, ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026, au lancement officiel du marché hebdomadaire de Yogo, dans le département de N’Gourti, une initiative communautaire qui ambitionne de dynamiser les activités économiques, de renforcer les échanges commerciaux transfrontaliers et de consolider les liens historiques de fraternité et de cohésion sociale entre les populations du Niger et du Tchad, rapporte l’agence nigerienne de presse. La cérémonie, organisée dans la localité de Yogo, a enregistré une forte mobilisation des autorités administratives, coutumières et religieuses, ainsi que des populations venues de différentes localités de la région de Diffa et de plusieurs provinces de la République du Tchad. Elle s’est déroulée en présence notamment du Conseiller spécial du Premier ministre, M. Issa Lemine, représentant le Chef du Gouvernement, de la Secrétaire générale adjointe de la Haute Autorité à la Consolidation de la Paix (HACP), des autorités administratives et coutumières tchadiennes, ainsi que de plusieurs chefs traditionnels venus des différentes régions du Niger et du pays voisin. Ont également pris part à cet événement l’ancien membre du Gouvernement, M. Mahaman Elhadji Ousman, les responsables des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), les représentants des services techniques déconcentrés de l’État, les leaders communautaires, les opérateurs économiques et plusieurs autres invités. Dans son allocution prononcée au nom du Gouverneur de la région de Diffa, le Général de Division Mahamadou Ibrahim Bagadoma, empêché, le SGA Mamane Gouzaé a souligné que «l’ouverture du marché de Yogo constitue une étape importante dans la promotion du développement économique local et l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations». Il a rappelé que «les marchés représentent bien plus que de simples espaces de commercialisation, puisqu’ils constituent également des lieux de rencontres, de solidarité, de brassage culturel et de renforcement de la cohésion sociale». Selon lui, dans une région comme Diffa, où les activités agro-sylvo-pastorales occupent une place essentielle dans les moyens de subsistance des populations, le développement des infrastructures marchandes constitue un levier important pour soutenir les producteurs, les éleveurs, les commerçants et les autres acteurs économiques. Le marché de Yogo, relate le représentant du Gouverneur, permettra de faciliter l’écoulement des productions locales, de rapprocher les vendeurs des acheteurs, de stimuler les échanges entre les différentes communautés et de créer de nouvelles opportunités économiques, notamment pour les femmes et les jeunes. M. Mamane Gouzaé a, par ailleurs, insisté sur la nécessité d’assurer une gestion responsable et concertée de cette infrastructure, en mettant un accent particulier sur l’hygiène, l’assainissement, le respect des règles de fonctionnement, la sécurité et la prévention des conflits. Il a également invité les populations à demeurer mobilisées aux côtés des autorités administratives et des Forces de défense et de sécurité pour préserver la paix et la sécurité, indispensables au développement des activités économiques. Prenant la parole à son tour, le Préfet du département de N’Gourti, le capitaine Issoufou Koraou, a salué la portée socioéconomique et stratégique de cette initiative, qu’il considère comme une véritable opportunité pour le développement de la commune rurale de N’Gourti. Il a particulièrement mis en avant la position géographique de Yogo, qui en fait un carrefour commercial transfrontalier susceptible de favoriser les échanges entre les différentes communes de la région de Diffa et les localités frontalières du Tchad. Pour le Préfet, ce marché contribuera à la valorisation des produits agro-pastoraux et artisanaux, à l’amélioration de la résilience des acteurs économiques et au raffermissement des liens séculaires de fraternité entre les populations des deux pays. Il a également souligné que cette infrastructure constituera une source supplémentaire de recettes pour la commune, permettant de soutenir la réalisation des actions de développement au profit des populations. À cet effet, il a exhorté les autorités communales à mettre en place des mécanismes appropriés pour garantir une gestion concertée et transparente du marché ainsi qu’une mobilisation conséquente des ressources internes. De son côté, le Conseiller spécial du Premier ministre, M. Issa Lemine, représentant le Chef du Gouvernement, a salué cette initiative qui traduit la volonté des populations de prendre une part active dans leur propre développement. Il a relevé que le marché de Yogo constitue une infrastructure à vocation économique, mais également un puissant instrument de rapprochement entre les communautés nigériennes et tchadiennes. Il a notamment encouragé les populations à préserver cet acquis collectif, à faire de Yogo un espace d’échanges pacifiques et de prospérité partagée, tout en invitant les autorités locales, les chefs traditionnels et les acteurs économiques à accompagner durablement cette dynamique. M. Issa lemine a enfin réaffirmé l’importance de telles initiatives communautaires dans la consolidation de la paix, de la solidarité et de l’intégration entre les populations vivant de part et d’autre de la frontière. Pour sa part, l’Administrateur délégué sortant de la commune rurale de N’Gourti a exprimé sa satisfaction quant à l’aboutissement de cette initiative, qu’il a présentée comme un événement majeur pour l’avenir socioéconomique du groupement de Yogo et de l’ensemble du département. Il a indiqué que le marché ne constitue pas uniquement un lieu de transactions commerciales, mais également un espace de solidarité, de brassage social et de rapprochement entre les communautés. Il a, à cet effet, invité les commerçants, les usagers et les responsables du marché à faire preuve de civisme, de discipline et de responsabilité pour garantir sa bonne gestion, son entretien et sa pérennité. L’un des moments forts de cette cérémonie a été l’intervention du Chef de groupement Toubou Kedelaya de Yogo, l’Honorable Hamet Kedella Botrane,lu par son représentant ,M. Baba kadella Boutrane qui a livré un message particulièrement axé sur la fraternité, l’unité et la préservation des liens historiques entre les communautés du Niger et du Tchad. Dans une adresse empreinte d’émotion, il a chaleureusement remercié les autorités nigériennes et les nombreuses délégations tchadiennes ayant effectué le déplacement à Yogo pour prendre part à cet événement. S’adressant particulièrement aux chefs traditionnels et aux autorités venus du Tchad, il a rappelé que les populations vivant de part et d’autre de la frontière partagent une histoire commune, des liens de parenté, des traditions, des alliances matrimoniales et des relations sociales profondément enracinées. « La frontière est sur le papier, mais dans nos cœurs, il n’y a jamais eu de frontière », a-t-il notamment souligné, pour illustrer la profondeur des liens qui unissent ces communautés. Pour le Chef de groupement, le marché de Yogo est justement appelé à devenir un espace où les familles se retrouvent, où les communautés renouent leurs relations et où les échanges commerciaux contribuent à entretenir cette fraternité historique. Il a également salué la vision des plus hautes autorités du Niger, notamment le Président de la République, Chef de l’État, le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani, ainsi que le Premier ministre, M. Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine, et l’accompagnement de la Haute Autorité à la Consolidation de la Paix. Il a particulièrement mis en avant la mobilisation communautaire ayant permis de concrétiser cette initiative, soulignant que les populations de Yogo ont elles-mêmes contribué à la réalisation de leur marché, dans un esprit de responsabilité et de participation au développement local. « À Yogo, tout le monde sera respecté. Tout le monde sera accueilli », a-t-il assuré, en précisant que ce marché est destiné à l’ensemble des populations, sans distinction d’origine ou de nationalité. Notons qu’auparavant, les représentants des associations des chefs traditionnels du Niger et de la délégation tchadienne ont également pris la parole pour saluer l’initiative et magnifier les relations historiques entre les communautés frontalières. Leurs différentes interventions ont convergé vers un même appel : faire du marché de Yogo un véritable espace de coexistence pacifique, de solidarité, de dialogue et de développement partagé. La présence remarquable des chefs traditionnels des deux pays a, à cet égard, témoigné de l’intérêt accordé à cette initiative et de la volonté des autorités coutumières de contribuer au renforcement de la coopération transfrontalière et à la consolidation de la paix dans cette partie de la région du Sahel. La cérémonie a également été marquée par plusieurs prestations artistiques et culturelles mettant en valeur les traditions et le patrimoine culturel de la zone, dans une ambiance de convivialité et de fraternité. À travers l’ouverture de ce marché hebdomadaire, la localité de Yogo entend ainsi renforcer son attractivité économique et devenir un important point de convergence pour les commerçants, les éleveurs, les producteurs et les populations des différentes localités du Niger et du Tchad. Au-delà de sa dimension commerciale, cette nouvelle infrastructure marchande porte donc une ambition plus large : celle de faire de l’activité économique un facteur de rapprochement des peuples, de consolidation de la paix et de renforcement du vivre-ensemble entre les communautés frontalières. L’ouverture du marché hebdomadaire de Yogo marque ainsi une nouvelle étape dans la dynamique de développement local du département de N’Gourti et dans la promotion de la coopération communautaire entre le Niger et le Tchad. items.title: Patrick Boamah challenges Finance Minister’s directive stopping monthly allowances for SOE board members
items.description: Okaikwei Central Member of Parliament Patrick Boamah has questioned the Finance Minister’s directive halting monthly sitting allowances for board members of state-owned enterprises (SOEs), describing the decision as worrying and calling for it to be reconsidered. Speaking during the debate on the 2027 Budget in Parliament on Thursday, November 19, 2026, Mr Boamah said the directive could affect the ability of state-owned companies and statutory institutions to hold regular board meetings. “Ato Forson has stopped payment of monthly allowances to board members of state-owned enterprises. This is worrying and must be reconsidered,” he said. The MP said a letter dated October 12, 2026, signed by the Deputy Minister of Finance on behalf of the Minister, had been sent to more than 164 companies and state-owned enterprises directing them to stop paying monthly sitting allowances to their directors. “There’s a letter written by the Deputy Minister of Finance on 12 October 2026 to over 164 companies or state-owned enterprises in this country, signed on behalf of the Minister of Finance, that they should henceforth stop paying monthly sitting allowances to companies or their directors,” he told Parliament. He argued that regular board meetings were necessary for effective governance and the growth of state-owned institutions. “These are state companies; these are statutory institutions that require regular board meetings to help grow those companies. But this is a directive by the Minister of Finance asking for board allowance not to be paid. And this is a very serious matter that must be looked into by the House,” he said. The directive forms part of the government’s efforts to reduce public expenditure and improve the efficiency of state-owned enterprises. Mr Boamah urged Parliament to examine the decision, particularly its implications for the oversight and operations of the affected institutions.

items.title: Chaima Issa en grève de la faim | ASF réclame sa libération immédiate
items.description: Face à l'entrée en grève de la faim illimitée de Chaima Issa, l'organisation Avocats sans frontières (ASF) a publié un communiqué appelant à sa libération immédiate. Depuis sa cellule, Chaima Issa observe une grève de la faim illimitée depuis le 16 novembre 2026 pour protester contre son maintien en détention. ASF a exprimé sa vive préoccupation, tout en demandant aux autorités pénitentiaires et judiciaires de veiller scrupuleusement à l'intégrité physique de l'activiste politique, condamnée à la lourde peine de 20 ans de prison dans l'affaire dite de « complot contre la sûreté de l'État ». Dans son communiqué, ASF a souligné la nécessité de lui assurer un accès continu aux soins ainsi qu'un suivi médical approprié tout au long de son mouvement de protestation. Pour rappel, Chaima Issa a décidé de mener cette grève de la faim pour dénoncer sa condamnation et s'était exprimée en ces termes : « La vie sans liberté n'est pas une vie ; c'est une mort lente où l'âme s'érode jour après jour, et nul ne peut accepter d'être privé de son droit à la liberté et à la dignité, puis qu'on lui demande de se taire comme si de rien n'était. » Y. items.title: NCCIA claims uncovering network allegedly involved in up to Rs1tr betting, money laundering
items.description: KARACHI: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Thursday claimed to have uncovered an extensive alleged financial network involved in illegal online betting and gambling, fraudulent business operations and suspected money laundering, with an estimated transaction exposure of up to approximately Rs1 trillion. Speaking at a press conference at his office, Karachi NCCIA Additional Director Shahzad Akbar said the investigation was initiated after suspicious financial activities were reported through the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), which revealed massive transactions across commercial banks, microfinance banks and digital wallets. Investigators identified an alleged organised network operating through online betting and gambling platforms, including 1XBet, Stake, X777, X555, 99c444, X111 and MelBet. The network allegedly collected gambling-related payments through digital channels, including two renowned mobile wallets, before routing the funds through multiple bank accounts, registered companies, fictitious business establishments and third-party account holders. “These arrangements were allegedly used to conceal the actual source, ownership and ultimate beneficiaries of the funds,” the NCCIA officer said. The investigation also came across suspected fraudulent sub-merchant registrations, forged identity documents, fictitious businesses and accounts allegedly operated as rented or mule accounts. Billions in suspicious transactions unearthed According to NCCIA, a detailed financial analysis revealed exceptionally high transaction volumes in accounts allegedly associated with the network: Rs. 3.72 billion credited to one suspected settlement account within approximately 22 months Rs. 2.43bn credited to another company account. Rs. 1.97bn received through suspected rented or mule accounts. These transactions were found to be grossly disproportionate to the declared business activities and financial capacity of the respective account holders, the cybercrime agency said. The overall estimated transaction exposure may be up to approximately Rs1tr, highlighting the scale and complexity of the suspected financial network. In a significant financial enforcement operation, Karachi’s NCCIA secured approximately Rs1bn in suspected illicit funds across multiple financial accounts within a single day, preventing their further withdrawal, transfer or potential dissipation. “This action represents a major development in disrupting the financial infrastructure allegedly supporting the illegal betting and gambling network,” said the NCCIA additional director. Banking officials, company directors under probe The investigation has brought suspected banking officials, company directors, business operators, payment facilitators and account holders under scrutiny. According to a first information report (FIR), certain banking officials allegedly facilitated the continued operation of suspicious accounts despite anti-money laundering alerts and other warning indicators. “Their potential involvement and any institutional lapses are being examined through banking records, financial documentation and digital evidence,” Akbar said. NCCIA Karachi conducted coordinated raids at multiple premises and arrested several individuals allegedly involved in the network. The FIR, dated Nov 18, was registered under relevant provisions of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca), read with applicable provisions of the Pakistan Penal Code. The FIR was filed against 40 individuals and business entities, including 32 chief executive officers of companies and five suspects arrested in connection with the alleged offences. The NCCIA additional director claimed that most of those involved in online gambling by developing “different” apps were Chinese nationals. Last week, the NCCIA called for stricter regulations governing company registration and bank account verification, warning that loopholes in the existing system are being exploited by illegal call centres, online betting operators and international fraud networks to launder money and defraud victims. NCCIA Islamabad/Rawalpindi Additional Director Muhammad Shoaib Khan explained that fake companies were being registered through weak verification procedures, after which bank accounts opened in their names were linked to loan applications, betting and gaming portals to receive and transfer illicit funds.

items.title: Le gouvernement veut renforcer les mesures pour protéger le pouvoir d’achat
items.description: La cheffe du gouvernement, Fatima Zahra El Mansouri, a présidé jeudi à Rabat la deuxième réunion de la commission interministérielle consacrée à la protection du pouvoir d’achat des citoyens. Au centre des discussions : la stabilisation des prix des produits de première nécessité, notamment les légumes et les viandes, ainsi que l’amélioration des conditions d’approvisionnement des marchés nationaux. À l’ouverture de cette réunion, Fatima Zahra El Mansouri a réaffirmé que la préservation du pouvoir d’achat constituait une priorité majeure de l’action gouvernementale. Elle a souligné que l’exécutif suivait de près l’évolution des prix et la situation de l’approvisionnement dans les différents marchés du Royaume, tout en privilégiant des interventions anticipées pour corriger les éventuels dysfonctionnements susceptibles d'affecter le quotidien des ménages. Concernant les légumes, les discussions ont porté sur les moyens de renforcer l’offre et de garantir la disponibilité de ces produits sur les marchés intérieurs à des prix abordables. Le gouvernement entend notamment accorder la priorité à l’approvisionnement du marché national et à son équilibre, tout en envisageant une réorganisation des circuits de distribution et une réduction du nombre d’intermédiaires afin de limiter les hausses injustifiées des prix. S’agissant des viandes, la commission a procédé à une évaluation de la situation du marché, en mettant l’accent sur la nécessité d’encadrer les circuits de commercialisation pour renforcer la transparence et favoriser la stabilité des prix. Les efforts visant à reconstituer et à soutenir le cheptel national devront également se poursuivre, avec pour objectif de garantir la pérennité de la production nationale et de répondre aux besoins de la consommation intérieure à moyen et long terme. À l’issue de la réunion, la cheffe du gouvernement a appelé les différents départements ministériels, les autorités locales et les services de contrôle à maintenir leur mobilisation sur le terrain et à renforcer leur coordination afin d’assurer la mise en œuvre immédiate des mesures retenues. Cette réunion s’est tenue en présence des ministres de l’Intérieur, de l’Économie et des Finances, de l’Agriculture, de la Pêche maritime et du Développement rural, ainsi que de l’Industrie et du Commerce, en plus du secrétaire général du gouvernement et du ministre délégué chargé de la Pêche maritime. items.title: West Africa leans towards three-country plan for regional payment system, Liberia central bank chief says
items.description: West African central banks are leaning towards splitting the hosting of the region’s planned payment and settlement system among three institutions so that no single economy dominates it, Liberia’s central bank governor said, as the bloc puts in place the financial plumbing for its long-delayed single currency. The ECOWAS Payment and Settlement System (EPSS), being built by the West African Monetary Agency (WAMA), is designed to link the region’s national payment networks through a regional instant payment system (IPS) and a wholesale real-time gross settlement (RTGS) platform. Central Bank of Liberia Executive Governor Henry F. Saamoi said a consultant who assessed the project recommended that Nigeria host the instant payment component because of its experience, that the Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) in Senegal run the RTGS because it already operates a payment system for eight countries, and that Ghana operate the backup site. He said discussions were ongoing. “I like the three-country approach because we are a region, we are a bloc,” Saamoi told JoyNews in an interview on Wednesday in Balaclava, Mauritius. “Having just one country dominate the payment system, for me I have some issues.” He said the region’s central bank governors had agreed that each member state should first build its own national system, “so that at that point in time we are all able to integrate seamlessly to facilitate cross-border payments.” At their meeting in Monrovia on February 12, 2026, the governors mandated WAMA to recruit an independent external consultant to assess the hosting bids. WAMA documents show that Ghana’s GhIPSS and Nigeria’s NIBSS have expressed interest in hosting parts of the infrastructure. Saamoi spoke a day before the AfricaNenda Foundation launched its fifth State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa (SIIPS) report in Mauritius on Thursday, November 19, 2026. The report is published in partnership with the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and the World Bank Group. The report says EPSS would not simply duplicate existing infrastructure. It would give the eight members of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU), which already share a regional instant payment rail, connections across the wider ECOWAS bloc that their own system cannot offer. It warned, however, that parallel systems built without common standards could raise costs and deepen fragmentation. “The risk lies not in the overlap itself but in a lack of coordination,” the report said. DOLLAR SETTLEMENT Payments between West African countries are still often settled in U.S. dollars, which traders and analysts describe as a costly obstacle to trade within the region. Saamoi said ECOWAS had not yet chosen a base currency for settling payments on EPSS. For now, member states are joining the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), which settles in local currencies. “Ideally, we should follow exactly what PAPSS is doing currently,” he said. The West African Monetary Institute is studying how to manage exchange rate risk among member states and will report to the governors. West African leaders have reaffirmed their commitment to launching the Eco in 2027 under a phased approach that will allow only member states meeting the bloc’s convergence criteria to join at the start. Saamoi said central bankers meeting in Abidjan were expected to reach a decision by Friday that would guide their preparations for the launch. He said cost would decide whether the regional system succeeds. “Instant payment comes along with the caveat of affordability,” he said. “If the citizen in whose interest you are deploying an IPS cannot afford it, then of course it’s not going to be used.” LIBERIA’S FAST BUILD Liberia launched its first instant payment system, Pay Na-Na, on December 16, 2025, linking the country’s two mobile money operators, Lone Star MTN and Orange Liberia. The central bank says the system was delivered in 73 business days, and Saamoi said he had been told no other country had moved as fast. Transactions on the platform already run into the millions, worth millions of U.S. dollars and billions of Liberian dollars, he said, and civil servants now receive their salaries in real time “without any deductions.” The central bank plans to launch a National Electronic Payment Switch by the end of the first quarter of 2027 to connect commercial banks, which cannot yet send money to one another instantly. “In the comfort of your bed you are able to do transaction from bank A to bank B. Today that doesn’t work,” Saamoi said. Donors financed the system, which runs on open-source software. Saamoi said a hackathon in early December would train local firms to support it so that the country does not depend on outside help. Liberia’s financial inclusion rate stands at 52%, and the bank is aiming for 75% by the end of 2029. CONTINENTAL PICTURE The SIIPS 2026 report counts 39 live instant payment systems providing functionality for 43 African countries as of July 2026. They processed 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, and volumes grew by an average of 28% a year between 2021 and 2025. The average transaction fell from $45 in 2021 to $26 in 2025, a sign that people are using the systems for smaller, everyday payments. For the first time, the report estimates the economic effect of these systems. Countries that launched one saw active account usage rise by about 7 percentage points compared with countries that did not, and GDP per capita about 17% higher in the years after launch. AfricaNenda describes the results as early and directional. “The question now is not whether instant payment systems contribute value,” AfricaNenda Chief Executive Robert Ochola wrote in the report’s foreword. COUNTRY BY COUNTRY The report ranks each system on an inclusivity spectrum with three levels: basic, progressed and mature. NIGERIA. The NIBSS Instant Payment (NIP) system remains the only one in Africa rated mature. It is the mandatory rail for transfers between all licensed institutions, including mobile money operators, and charges a low flat fee per transaction. In a survey of 78 Nigerian small businesses, 72% said they now serve customers they could not reach before, 63% restock more often and 56% spend less time counting cash. Nigeria’s eNaira digital currency is rated basic. GHANA. GhIPSS Instant Pay was reclassified this year as a cross-domain system, meaning banks, mobile money operators and fintechs can all pay one another directly. Both it and Ghana Mobile Money Interoperability are rated progressed. In March 2026, GhIPSS, the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department and 24 commercial banks signed an agreement making the GhIPSS-GIFMIS rail the only authorised channel for government payments to suppliers and third parties. WAEMU. In the bloc of Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Togo, the BCEAO launched the PI-SPI regional system on September 30, 2025. It entered the ranking at progressed, and the report calls it a milestone for cross-border retail payments in Africa. Eighty institutions had connected by July 31, 2026, ahead of a September 30, 2026 deadline, although use is so far concentrated in Senegal and Côte d’Ivoire. LIBERIA. Pay Na-Na entered the ranking at basic. It is one of three systems in Africa built entirely on the open-source Mojaloop platform, and it started with government-to-person and person-to-person payments. GUINEA. The central bank launched NimbaPay on July 22, 2026. It is also built on Mojaloop and entered the ranking at basic. It handles only person-to-person payments for now, with payments to government and cross-border transfers planned for later phases. SIERRA LEONE. The Salone Payment Switch moved up to basic this year after adding new uses. THE GAMBIA. The Gamswitch interbank system is rated basic and is one of a handful of large systems behind the fast growth of bank-only systems across Africa. A successor platform, BANTABA 2.0, is in development. CABO VERDE. The STII system has completed a pilot phase. Cabo Verde and The Gambia sit outside WAEMU, and the report says their regional connections will come through EPSS.

items.title: Dak’Art 2026 : Bassirou Diomaye Faye fait de la culture une « superstructure de souveraineté »
items.description: Au Cap Manuel, jeudi 19 novembre, Bassirou Diomaye Faye a ouvert la 16e édition de la Biennale de l'Art africain contemporain. Dans l'ancien palais de Justice, le chef de l'État a plaidé pour une culture érigée en pilier de souveraineté, créatrice d’emplois et de richesse, et pour un continent qui reprend la main sur son récit. Un geste de résistance Le Président a d'abord justifié le maintien de l'événement, malgré « un contexte exigeant ». Sa formule est nette : « On ne suspend pas la respiration d'un peuple au motif que les temps sont durs. C'est au contraire dans ces moments-là qu'une Nation a le plus besoin de ses artistes. » Après le succès des Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse, dont il a salué les artisans, il a vu dans cette Biennale la suite du même récit : « Le monde a vu ce que l'Afrique sait faire lorsqu'elle se raconte elle-même. » L'(anti) fragilité, thème de l'édition Le thème retenu par le Comité d'orientation, « (anti) fragilité », sonne selon lui « comme un acte de résistance philosophique ». Le chef de l'État a décrit une parenthèse qui « sépare et relie dans le même geste », laissant voir la fragilité tout en annonçant son dépassement. Il y a lu une réponse à ce que « le système-monde a voulu nous assigner comme destin » : fragilité économique, climatique, démocratique. L'Afrique, a-t-il dit, ne veut plus se plaindre de ses « retards » mais prendre conscience de ses forces. Puis cette phrase, qui résume la philosophie de la Biennale : « De la contrainte, l'Art africain fait une forme. Du manque, il fait une œuvre. » Le Président a rattaché ce message à l'actualité mondiale, entre les musées interpellés sur l'origine de leurs collections et l'intelligence artificielle qui interroge « ce qui, dans la création, demeure irréductiblement humain ». La RDC à l'honneur Pays invité d'honneur, la République démocratique du Congo a reçu un hommage appuyé, en présence de sa ministre de la Culture, Yolande Elebe Ma Ndembo. Pour le chef de l'État, ce choix est « une évidence artistique, autant qu'une évidence fraternelle ». Il a salué des créateurs qui rappellent « qu'on peut tout prendre à un peuple, sauf sa capacité à créer de la beauté et donc à inventer le monde ». Écrire sa propre histoire de l'Art Le cœur du discours est politique. Le Président défend « une vision de souveraineté culturelle pleine et entière » : « Trop longtemps, d'autres ont écrit cette histoire à notre place. Aujourd'hui, plus que jamais, il nous faut nous-mêmes écrire notre propre histoire de l'Art, avec nos mots, nos critères et nos institutions. » Dans l'Agenda national de Transformation Sénégal 2050, la culture change de statut. Elle n'est plus, a-t-il affirmé, « seulement un supplément d'âme, mais une superstructure de souveraineté, au même titre que l'environnement, nos routes et notre énergie ». Elle forge l'identité et la cohésion sociale, mais elle « crée de la valeur et des revenus » et « offre des emplois à notre jeunesse ». Un marché commun de l'art africain Le Président a chiffré l'enjeu : l'Afrique capte moins de 1 % du marché mondial de l'art. « Ce chiffre n'est pas une fatalité. Il est la mesure de l'espace qui s'ouvre devant nous. » Il a annoncé son souhait de soutenir, avec l'Union africaine, un marché commun de l'art africain, dans le prolongement de la ZLECAF. L'image est restée : « Une œuvre créée à Kinshasa doit pouvoir être exposée à Dakar et acquise à Nairobi sans rencontrer plus d'obstacles qu'un sac de cacao ou un baril de pétrole. » Les lauréats, « nouveaux visages de l'antifragilité » Il a enfin remercié les équipes de la Biennale, puis félicité les lauréats, du Grand Prix Léopold Sédar Senghor au Prix Révélation du jeune créateur. Il y voit « les nouveaux visages de l'antifragilité », chargés de porter les couleurs d'une génération qui entend « faire de l'épreuve une matière à création ». Avant de déclarer ouverte Dak'Art 2026, qui se tient jusqu'au 19 décembre, il a lancé : « Que vive l'art africain ! Que vive Dakar, capitale de la création ! »

items.title: International Men’s Day: Seven in 10 Ghanaian men have experienced violence in their lifetime – Gender Ministry
items.description: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has raised concerns about the health, mental well-being and exposure to violence among men and boys in Ghana, citing findings that about seven in 10 men have experienced at least one form of violence in their lifetime. The Ministry said the figures highlighted the need for greater attention to men’s welfare, stronger support systems and a collective effort to promote positive masculinity and build a violence-free society. In a statement to mark International Men’s Day on Wednesday, November 19, the Ministry said men continued to face significant challenges, including preventable diseases, occupational hazards, mental health difficulties and violence, many of which remained underreported. It noted that although men were often expected to demonstrate strength and provide for their families, the pressures associated with these expectations could have serious consequences for their physical and mental well-being. International Men’s Day is observed annually on November 19 to recognise the positive contributions of men and boys, promote positive male role models and draw attention to issues affecting their health and welfare. The Ministry said the 2026 celebration was being held under the global theme, “The Future Is Everyone” , which emphasises the importance of collective responsibility in achieving gender equality and building a fairer, healthier and safer society. It stressed that gender equality should not be viewed as a contest between men and women but as a shared responsibility requiring the participation of everyone. Highlighting the health challenges confronting men, the Ministry said a boy born in Ghana today could expect to live approximately 63.7 years, nearly five years less than a girl, whose life expectancy stands at about 68.6 years. It attributed much of the disparity to late health-seeking behaviour, risky lifestyles, occupational hazards and preventable diseases. The Ministry also expressed concern about the mental health burden among men, particularly the pressure to provide for their families and the stigma associated with financial difficulties and unemployment. Citing studies based on World Health Organisation data, it said suicide rates among men in Ghana were higher than those among women in every year between 2000 and 2019, with older men being the most affected. It further referenced research by the University of Ghana, which found that suicidal behaviour in the country was largely a male problem, closely linked to societal expectations for men to act as providers and the shame many experience when they lose their jobs or sources of income. The Ministry recalled Ghana’s 2023 decision to decriminalise attempted suicide, describing it as an important step towards ensuring that people experiencing psychological distress receive care rather than punishment. It called for sustained efforts to build on the progress and encourage men to seek help when confronted with emotional and mental health difficulties. The statement also drew attention to violence against men, citing a national study on domestic violence conducted by the Ghana Statistical Service and its partners. According to the Ministry, the study found that approximately seven in 10 men had experienced at least one form of violence in their lifetime, while one in five had experienced domestic violence within the preceding 12 months. It added that men reported higher levels of physical violence than women, with most of the incidents occurring outside the home. However, the Ministry emphasised that men also had a critical responsibility to help end violence against women and girls. Citing the 2022 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey, it said two in five women who had ever been in a relationship had experienced emotional, physical or sexual violence at the hands of a partner. It further noted that about one in 10 men still believed that a husband was justified in beating his wife under certain circumstances. The Ministry said the statistics demonstrated the interconnected nature of the well-being of men, women and children, warning that neglecting the welfare of men and boys had consequences for entire families and communities. It advocated positive masculinity, characterised by care, respect and responsibility, as an important tool for tackling violence and promoting peaceful homes and communities. As part of its recommendations, the Ministry urged men and boys to prioritise their health by undertaking regular medical check-ups and speaking openly about their challenges. It stressed that seeking help should be regarded as a sign of strength rather than weakness. It also encouraged men to become positive role models who reject violence at home, in workplaces and within their communities. Families were urged to raise boys who could express their emotions, respect women and girls, and participate in household responsibilities. The Ministry further called on families to pay greater attention to the welfare of men in their lives and regularly check on their well-being. Traditional and religious leaders were encouraged to use their platforms to promote positive masculinity and condemn all forms of violence. Employers were also urged to prioritise workplace health, safety and mental well-being while creating conditions that enable fathers to play active roles in their children’s lives. The Ministry called on the media and civil society organisations to highlight positive male role models and help break the silence surrounding men’s physical health, mental health and experiences of violence. The Ministry reminded survivors of violence, irrespective of their gender, that they were protected under the Domestic Violence Act, 2007 (Act 732). It urged victims to report abuse to the Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU) of the Ghana Police Service or the nearest Department of Social Welfare office. It also provided the following support contacts: Orange Support Centre (toll-free): 0800 111 222 Orange Support Centre (WhatsApp): 055 175 7575 Helpline of Hope (toll-free): 0800 800 800 / 0800 900 900 DOVVSU: 0551000900 Police (toll-free): 18555 Looking ahead to the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence, which begins on November 25, the Ministry called on men and boys across the country to participate as allies and champions in the campaign. It encouraged Ghanaians to share messages promoting men’s health, positive masculinity and violence prevention using the hashtags #InternationalMensDay, #TheFutureIsEveryone and #ViolenceFreeGhana. The Ministry reaffirmed its appreciation for the contributions of men and boys to national development, stressing that their health, voices and examples mattered in building a peaceful society. “Together, let us build a Ghana where every man, woman, boy and girl lives in dignity, safety and peace,” it said.

items.title: L’entreprise Boya aménage deux ronds-points à Ngor et Almadies
items.description: Les quartiers de Ngor et Almadies étrennent deux ronds-points aménagés grâce à la société Boya Sa, filiale du groupe Fortuna Mining. Cette entreprise a procédé, aujourd’hui, à l’inauguration des aménagements réalisés sur deux ronds-points situés aux Almadies et à Ngor (Dakar Yoff), dans le cadre de sa collaboration avec le ministère de l’Environnement et de la Transition écologique, à travers l’initiative Responsabilité Sociétale des Entreprises – Plus Environnement (Rse+). Selon le communiqué parvenu à notre rédaction, hier, à travers l’aménagement de ces deux espaces publics, Boya Sa contribue à l’embellissement de zones stratégiques de la capitale. Seydina Alioune Ndjim, Directeur des Paysages urbains et des Espaces publics, a salué l’engagement de Boya Sa, qui à travers son accompagnement pour l’aménagement des deux ronds-points, pose un acte fort de responsabilité sociétale et environnementale. « Au-delà de cette contribution, c’est aussi l’expression d’une vision, d’un engagement citoyen et d’une volonté de participer à la transformation de notre environnement urbain », a dit M. Ndjim. Selon le document, lancée par le ministère de l’Environnement et de la Transition écologique, l’initiative Rse+ Environnement vise à renforcer la participation des entreprises au développement local et communautaire, tout en encourageant des actions concrètes en faveur de l’amélioration du cadre de vie et de la durabilité environnementale. Elle repose sur une dynamique de partenariat entre l’État et le secteur privé, afin de mobiliser les engagements volontaires des entreprises au service de l’intérêt collectif. Oumar KANDE

Al rato, unos 300 simpatizantes arropan a la exalcaldesa de Barcelona; varios jóvenes le piden selfis y Colau improvisa un mitin junto a los cabezas de lista de la provincia, que han armado una coalición autonómica independiente de la alianza en el resto del país, y pelean por llegar a cinco diputados para conformar un grupo propio valenciano en el Congreso. items.title: Burkina: Yamlaneba Ramdé appréhendé par la police
items.description: La Police nationale du Burkina Faso qui avait lancé, un peu plus tôt dans la journée de ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026, un avis de recherche contre Ramdé Yamlaneba, un enseignant né le 17 juillet 1968 à Imansgo, dans la province du Boulkiemdé, informe l'opinion que l'intéressé a été appréhendé. « Par une publication en date de ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026 sur sa page Facebook, la Police Nationale émettait un avis de recherche et lançait par la même occasion un appel afin d'aider ses services à appréhender le nommé RAMDE YAMLANEBA, auteur de multiples faits d'escroquerie, d'abus de confiance et de blanchiment de capitaux. Grâce à la forte mobilisation de tous et au concours des autres Forces de Défense et de Sécurité (FDS), en particulier la Police Municipale, l'auteur a été localisé et appréhendé à Koudougou, chef-lieu de la région de Nando, soit seulement trois (03) heures environ après la publication de l’avis de recherche. La Police Nationale réitère sa gratitude à la Police Municipale de Koudougou pour son soutien inestimable. Elle salue encore une fois la promptitude des citoyens et de l’ensemble des FDS, et les remercie pour leur collaboration, toute chose qui a permis l'arrestation du susnommé. Cette action vient réaffirmer le ferme engagement de tous autour de la résolution des problèmes de sécurité. Vive cette collaboration ! Ensemble, nous pouvons bouter l'insécurité hors de nos cités ! » La Police Nationale, une force publique au service des citoyens ! L’article Burkina: Yamlaneba Ramdé appréhendé par la police est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, top UN court rules
items.description: Myanmar has been found guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority by the International Court of Justice (ICJ). The verdict marks the first time a state has ever been found to have committed genocide by an international court. Yuji Iwasawa, president of the UN’s top court, said Myanmar had the “intention to destroy” a substantial part of the Rohingya population and engaged in “extensive destruction of evidence” to hide its crimes. A military crackdown in 2017 killed thousands of Rohingya and forced more than 700,000 to flee Buddhist-majority Myanmar, formerly known as Burma. Myanmar denied the claims against it, saying its forces had responded to attacks by armed groups. The court found on Thursday that “genocidal intent is the only reasonable inference that can be drawn from the evidence” it had seen. The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world. The ICJ also found in favour by majority that Myanmar had violated several other parts of the 1948 Genocide Convention. The case brought by The Gambia centred around so-called “clearance operations” initiated in 2017 in Rakhine State, where many of the Rohingya Muslim minority resided. After fighters from the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (Arsa) launched deadly attacks on more than 30 police posts there, Myanmar troops, backed by local Buddhist mobs, launched a wave of violence, prompting a mass exodus of Rohingya. Refugees recounted entire villages being burned down and the mass killing of civilians, while numerous survivors and eyewitnesses provided testimony that the Myanmar military had also raped and abused Rohingya women and girls. The ICJ determined that around 10,000 Rohingya were “violently killed” during the clearance operation, while more than 700,000 are thought to have fled to Bangladesh by foot or by sea. The court found that approximately 815,000 had been targeted in some way. Iwasawa said Myanmar’s military engaged in “indiscriminate” killings, the execution of men, “widespread” sexual violence, “extreme violence” against children and the deliberate burning of Rohingya homes. He said the military had also attacked Rohingya as they were fleeing to Bangladesh. Myanmar, he added, had engaged in “extensive destruction of evidence” by burning or disposing of bodies, burned and bulldozed sites that were cleared and failed to prosecute those who had perpetrated the acts of violence. While the ICJ recognised the role Arsa played, it found there was “overlap” between an “anti-Rohingya hate speech campaign” – which portrayed the Rohingya as “sub-human” and “a violent threat” – and the clearance operations that made violence against the population more likely. Myanmar consistently denied genocide against the Rohingya, saying its operations had targeted militant or insurgent threats in response to the Arsa attacks. In January, government representative Ko Ko Hlaing told the ICJ that the country “was not obliged to remain idle and allow terrorists to have free reign”. He said he had “no comment” following Thursday’s verdict. The ICJ also looked at the wider treatment of Rohingya leading up to the clearance operation and found that policies like limiting married couples to two children were discriminatory and aimed to erode their rights. It said Myanmar had an obligation to pay proportionate reparations, but said an exact figure could be determined at a later date. ‘Recognition of our suffering’ The court’s decision was welcomed by Rohingya communities and human rights groups. “This is like formal recognition of our suffering,” says Mohammed Nowkim, a Rohingya who was driven out of Rakhine in 2017 and now lives in Canada. “The Rohingya have been waiting for justice for decades.” Human Rights Watch said the ruling was “long-awaited recognition of the suffering the Rohingya have endured”. Meanwhile, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said the “suffering, misery and humiliation” inflicted on the Rohingya people was a “stain on the conscience of humanity”. He added that the court’s decision “must now translate into real action”. To implicate the Myanmar government in genocide, the court had to determine not just that terrible acts had been committed, but that there was an intent on the part of officials or arms of the state to partially or completely destroy the group. Thursday’s ruling is without precedent. Myanmar now carries the stain of being the first state to have been found to have violated the 1948 Genocide Convention. The ICJ has only twice before ruled on claims of state-backed genocide in the years since the Genocide Convention was signed in the aftermath of the Holocaust, in both cases finding there was insufficient evidence to attribute the actions to the state. Dozens of individuals have been found guilty of genocide, but finding their actions were at the direct behest of the state requires a higher evidential bar to prove genocide, the gravest of crimes under international law. Philippe Sands KC, a top human rights lawyer who helped bring the case, described it as an “historic judgment”. He told BBC Radio 4’s World at One programme that it was “right up there with the great moments of international justice: Nuremberg, Pinochet, and others”, referring to the trials of Nazi leaders following World War Two and that of the Chilean dictator, respectively. However, the ICJ is not a criminal court and its powers of enforcement are limited. It cannot send military officials to prison, while it relies on the UN Security Council and political pressure to impose its rulings. The ruling will, though, have implications for other genocide cases pending with the ICJ, including one brought by South Africa against Israel over its war in Gaza. Sands said that pending case had been the “elephant in the room” during the Myanmar hearings. He added that, while ruling against Myanmar did not mean the court would find similarly with Gaza, if it had not found Myanmar responsible, the case against Israel “would, in effect, be over”. Israel says the case against it is “wholly unfounded”. Antonia Mulvey, executive director of Legal Action Worldwide, told the BBC that the court had not accepted Myanmar’s counter-terrorism defence and had found for the first time that rape and sexual violence was an act of genocide, positions it would bear in mind for future cases. Following Thursday’s ruling, UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the government was ordering Myanmar’s defence attaché be expelled and that he was summoning its charge d’affaires. He pledged to set out “further action in the coming days to ensure those responsible are held to account” after a cross-party group of MPs called for the government to resume sanctions against Myanmar’s military.

items.title: Pru-East MP links recurring typhoid cases to broken water system, calls for urgent rehabilitation
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Pru-East, Emmanuel Kwaku Boam, has told Parliament that typhoid is ravaging communities in his constituency due to lack of access to potable water. He said the situation has escalated to cases of intestinal perforation, the acutest form of typhoid, which he described as a very big deal for the area. Mr Boam raised the alarm when he asked the Minister for Works, Housing and Water Resources about the state of the request for water supply intervention for the Parambo-Sawaba community, which had been submitted to the Community Water and Sanitation Agency (CWSA). He said the crisis is not limited to Parambo-Sawaba alone, but affects about 99 communities in the Pru-East area, with residents forced to rely on unsafe water sources. According to him, the affected enclave has a population of close to 50,000 people, while the wider catchment is estimated at over 500,000. He said the health emergency, which dates back to 2022/2023, has persisted for years, with residents suffering repeated bouts of typhoid linked to the water they drink. Mr Boam said although other interventions are ongoing, the core problem remains the water table and hard water in the area, and the rehabilitation of the water systems remains the only sustainable way to stop the infections. Minister Admits System Is Down Responding, the Minister admitted that the Parambo-Sawaba Water System is currently non-functional. He said the CWSA is undertaking a comprehensive technical evaluation of the facility as part of an ongoing nationwide assessment of ninety-eight (98) broken-down water systems to determine the scope of rehabilitation works required. He assured the House that upon completion of the assessment, the CWSA intends to prioritise the Parambo-Sawaba system for rehabilitation and include it among the first batch of facilities to be considered for reconstruction. He added that the Ministry has been informed of a possible financial intervention from a financial institution through the Pru East District Assembly, and that the assessment results together with a priced Bill of Quantities will be shared with the Assembly to facilitate timely rehabilitation. Mr Boam, however, insisted that with typhoid and intestinal perforation already taking a toll, the intervention cannot wait any longer.

items.title: IET-Ghana honours Adom News journalist Kodwo Mensah Aboroampa at 40th anniversary
items.description: Adom News journalist Kodwo Mensah Aboroampa (Amos Kwofie) of the Multimedia Group has been honoured by the Institution of Engineering and Technology, Ghana (IET-GH), in recognition of his outstanding contribution to journalism and the promotion of engineering excellence in the country. The award was presented at the institution’s 40th anniversary celebration, held under the theme, “ Engineering Excellence for Sustainable National Development ”. The honour recognises Mr Aboroampa’s consistent media advocacy, which the institution says has helped increase the visibility of IET-GH, promote the engineering profession and raise public awareness of critical infrastructure and national development issues. In a citation presented to him, IET-GH praised his exceptional professionalism, dedication and invaluable service to the engineering fraternity. The citation specifically acknowledged his role in using journalism to highlight issues affecting the engineering sector and bring important conversations on infrastructure and national development to public attention. The citation read: IN HONOUR OF MR AMOS KWOFIE (KODWO MENSAH ABOROAMPA) “In recognition of your outstanding contribution to journalism and dedicated promotion of engineering excellence in Ghana. “Your consistent media advocacy has enhanced the visibility of IET-GH, promoted the engineering profession and raised public awareness of critical infrastructure and national development issues. “The Institution of Engineering and Technology, Ghana (IET-GH), proudly honours you for your exceptional professionalism, dedication and invaluable service to the engineering fraternity.” The citation was presented on November 20, 2026, by the President of IET-GH, Engr Wonder S. Davor, F.PE. Mr Aboroampa was among several distinguished personalities honoured at the ceremony, including President John Mahama, the Ga Mantse, Minister for Works, Housing and Water Resources Ahmed Ibrahim, and the immediate past President of IET-GH, Engineer Henry Kwadwo Boateng. The recognition adds to the journalist’s contribution to public-interest reporting, particularly in amplifying issues of national importance and promoting conversations that support Ghana’s development. The 40th anniversary celebration brought together key stakeholders to reflect on the engineering profession’s contribution to national development and the need for stronger collaboration in building sustainable infrastructure. IET-GH’s recognition of Mr Aboroampa also underscores the important role of the media in promoting professional excellence, accountability and public understanding of the engineering sector.
